description:
Satvis is a free, open-source satellite tracker for the Mac, also on iPhone and iPad. It draws more than 16,000 satellites on a 3D globe in real time: Starlink, GPS, weather satellites, the ISS and many more. Set your location and it predicts when each one passes overhead. The sky view shows the sky from where you stand. Drag to look around and see the satellites in each direction.

WHAT IT DOES
• Visualize satellites on a 3D globe in real time, propagated on the Mac with SGP4 from CelesTrak's element sets
• Show points, labels, orbits, orbit tracks, ground tracks, sensor cones, 3D models and ground station links per satellite, colored by orbit class (LEO, MEO, GEO, HEO)
• Switch catalog groups on and off (Starlink, GNSS, weather, Earth observation, crewed stations), or search for a single satellite
• Select a satellite to see its orbit, its next passes over your locations and its spacecraft details: country, operator, manufacturer, bus, mass and size
• Track a satellite: the camera flies to it and follows it along its orbit
• Save your location or any point you pick on the map, then list the upcoming passes over it and get a notification before one starts
• Find satellites overhead in the ground-level sky view, aimed by dragging or with the arrow keys
• See which satellites you could spot: the sky view dims those in Earth's shadow, too far away or in a daylit sky
• View the globe in 3D or flattened to 2D, over the base map, star field and terrain you choose: satellite imagery, Earth at night or the day's VIIRS imagery
• Start from the featured views, bookmark your own, and share any view as a link: it opens the same view on satvis.space
• Made for the Mac: drag, scroll and pinch with the mouse or trackpad, keyboard shortcuts for the menu commands, and a window you can size as you like
• Keep using it offline, from the satellite data it last fetched

WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM
Element sets come from CelesTrak, refreshed several times a day, and are propagated on your Mac with SGP4. Spacecraft details come from Jonathan McDowell's GCAT.

FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
No account, no ads, no in-app purchases, on the Mac as on iPhone and iPad. Developed in the open at github.com/Flowm/satvis under the MIT license.
